extracted.intended_audience: graduate students and researchers in algebraic geometry (readers of Vakil's Foundations of Algebraic Geometry)
extracted.subtask_description: Definitions, equivalent criteria, and basic preservation/ construction results for ampleness, global generation, Spec and Proj (relative versions), and the Grassmannian; includes exercises and hints showing how to check these properties and construct the associated schemes. Geared to learners proving standard facts and building schemes via local-to-global gluing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Line bundle as difference of two very ample line bundles (16.6.F)
rubrics_metrics.description: For any invertible sheaf L on a projective A-scheme X, we can find two very ample invertible sheaves M and N such that L ≅ M ⊗ N^∨.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exercise: Use the previous exercise(s) as hinted. This gives a way to express arbitrary line bundles on a projective scheme as the tensor quotient of very ample ones (useful for embedding or comparing line bundles).

rubrics_metrics.name: Pullback of ample under finite morphism is ample (16.6.G)
rubrics_metrics.description: Suppose π : X → Y is a finite morphism of proper A-schemes, and L is an ample line bundle on Y. Then π^*L is ample on X.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hint/proof strategy: use Theorem 16.6.2(b) (global generation criterion). For a finite-type quasicoherent sheaf F on X, show F ⊗ (π^*L)^n is globally generated for n ≫ 0 by pulling back surjections coming from ampleness on Y and using affineness of π; pullback preserves tensor products (Theorem 16.3.7(9)). Note this generalizes to π quasiaffine (cf. EGA reference).

rubrics_metrics.name: Tensoring with ample or base-point-free yields ample (16.6.H)
rubrics_metrics.description: If L and M are invertible sheaves on a proper A-scheme X and L is ample, then L ⊗ M is ample provided M is either ample or base-point-free.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exercise: combine properties of ampleness and base-point-freeness; use characterization of ampleness in terms of powers giving embeddings or global generation criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Semiample definition (16.6.4)
rubrics_metrics.description: An invertible sheaf L is semiample if some tensor power of it is base-point-free.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Translation: ample means some power gives a closed embedding into projective space, semiample means some power gives a morphism to projective space (not necessarily an embedding). The text notes this notion will not be used further here but records definition for reference.

rubrics_metrics.name: Absolute ampleness via sections forming a base (16.6.5)
rubrics_metrics.description: For a quasicompact scheme X, an invertible sheaf L is ample if the open subsets X_f = {p ∈ X : f(p) ≠ 0}, as f runs over sections of L^n for n > 0, form a base for the topology of X (quasicompactness is part of the condition).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: on an affine scheme every invertible sheaf is ample; on a projective A-scheme O(1) is ample. This gives an 'absolute' notion of ampleness independent of a base morphism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equivalent conditions for ampleness — global generation criterion (Theorem 16.6.6(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: If L is an invertible sheaf on a quasicompact scheme X, then (b) 'X is quasiseparated, and for every finite type quasicoherent sheaf F, there exists n_0 such that for all n ≥ n_0, F ⊗ L^n is globally generated' is one of the equivalent characterizations of ampleness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this to check ampleness by verifying eventual global generation for all finite-type quasicoherent sheaves; this is the typical cohomological/global-generation perspective used in proofs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equivalent conditions for ampleness — topology generated by sections (Theorem 16.6.6(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: For L as above, (c) 'As f runs over the global sections of L^n (n > 0), the open subsets X_f = {p ∈ X : f(p) ≠ 0} form a base for the topology of X' is equivalent to ampleness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the version used to connect local affine neighborhoods cut out by sections to ampleness; it is closely related to the absolute ampleness statement and useful for constructing embeddings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equivalent conditions for ampleness — affine opens form a base (Theorem 16.6.6(c'))
rubrics_metrics.description: A related equivalent condition is (c') 'As f runs over global sections of L^n (n>0), those open subsets X_f which are affine form a base for the topology of X.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This refinement controls affineness of the standard opens and is used in proofs to produce affines from sections; the equivalence to (c) does not require properness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equivalent conditions for ampleness — Proj description (Theorem 16.6.6(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: Let S = ⊕_{n≥0} Γ(X,L^n). Then (d) 'the open sets X_f (with f homogeneous of positive degree) cover X and the associated map X → Proj S is an open embedding' is another equivalent condition for ampleness (warning: S need not be finite type).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part (d) implies X is separated; this connects ampleness to a Proj construction and shows how L gives a projective-type presentation of X.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ample ⇔ some power is very ample (standard fact)
rubrics_metrics.description: An invertible sheaf L is ample if and only if some tensor power L^N is very ample (i.e., gives a closed embedding into projective space).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the motivating equivalence: ampleness is characterized by existence of some power that embeds X. It underlies many exercises and the conclusion that powers of ample bundles eventually give embeddings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Powers and restriction properties of ampleness (16.6.J)
rubrics_metrics.description: (a) For a positive integer n, L is ample iff L^n is ample. (b) If X → Z is a closed embedding and L is ample on X, then L|_Z is ample on Z.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these permanence properties when checking ampleness after base change, restriction, or replacing by powers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transporting global generation/base-point-freeness/ampleness to relative situation (16.6.7)
rubrics_metrics.description: The notions of global generation, base-point-freeness, and ampleness can be relativized: one may define relatively very ample (π-very ample) line bundles and other relative versions with respect to a morphism π.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The text defers a detailed development until projective morphisms are defined, but signals that the absolute notions have natural analogues when working over a base.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grassmannian functor definition (16.7.0.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Grassmannian functor G(k,n) sends a scheme B to the set of locally free rank k quotients Q of O_B^n, up to isomorphism (equivalently, short exact sequences 0 → S → O_B^n → Q → 0 with S,Q locally free of ranks n-k and k).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This functorial definition emphasizes quotients rather than subobjects because kernels of surjections of locally free sheaves are locally free while cokernels of injections need not be; it is the correct moduli functor to represent the Grassmannian.

rubrics_metrics.name: Representability of Grassmannian via determinant loci (16.7.B/C)
rubrics_metrics.description: For each k-subset I ⊂ {1,...,n}, there is an open subfunctor G(k,n)_I where the corresponding k sections of Q are linearly independent; this locus is defined by the nowhere-vanishing of the determinant of the k×k submatrix consisting of the I columns. The open subfunctors cover G(k,n), and each G(k,n)_I is representable (in fact by A^{k(n−k)}), hence G(k,n) is representable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exercise: make the determinant condition precise in trivializing neighborhoods and check compatibility on overlaps; the standard construction exhibits G(k,n) as glued affines and yields smoothness and dimension counts over a field.

rubrics_metrics.name: Universal exact sequence / tautological quotient on Grassmannian (16.7.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: Over the Grassmannian G(k,n) there is a tautological exact sequence 0 → S → O_{G}^n → Q → 0 where Q is the universal rank-k quotient and S the kernel (locally free of rank n−k).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This universal sequence realizes the moduli property and is used in constructions like the Plücker map and Plücker relations; it is the incidence data that defines the Grassmannian geometrically.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plücker embedding and ∧^k construction (16.7.2)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applying ∧^k to the tautological surjection O^{(n)} → Q gives a surjection ∧^k O^{(n)} → det Q, yielding a morphism to P^{(n choose k)-1} (the Plücker embedding).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interpret the Plücker coordinates as determinants of k×k minors; this produces an explicit projective embedding and is the basis for the Plücker equations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plücker equations (16.7.3)
rubrics_metrics.description: There are quadratic relations among the k×k minors (Plücker coordinates), called the Plücker equations; these vanish on G(k,n) and (with more work) cut out the homogeneous ideal of the Grassmannian.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exercises illustrate these relations in examples (e.g., G(2,4) is cut out by a single quadratic relation in P^5). These equations are the algebraic constraints characterizing the image under the Plücker embedding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relative Spec universal property (17.1.2)
rubrics_metrics.description: Given a quasicoherent O_X-algebra B on a scheme X, Spec B → X is the X-scheme characterized by: for any X-morphism µ : W → X, X-morphisms W → Spec B correspond functorially to O_X-algebra maps α: B → µ_* O_W making the evident diagram commute.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This universal property generalizes the affine Spec construction and uniquely characterizes Spec B up to unique isomorphism; it enables 'affine over X' constructions and local computations on affine opens.

rubrics_metrics.name: Spec computed affine-locally and base-change behavior (17.1.3, 17.1.F)
rubrics_metrics.description: Spec B can be computed affine-locally: over an affine open Spec A ⊂ X, Spec B|_{Spec A} ≅ Spec Γ(Spec A, B). Spec behaves well under base change: for µ : Y → X, Y ×_X Spec B ≅ Spec µ^*B.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This allows constructing Spec B by gluing local Specs and shows that Spec is compatible with pulling back the sheaf of algebras.

rubrics_metrics.name: Total space of a locally free sheaf as Spec(Sym• F^∨) (17.1.4, 17.1.G)
rubrics_metrics.description: For a finite rank locally free sheaf F on X, the total space (vector bundle) of F is Spec(Sym• F^∨); locally around a point p there is an open U with Spec(Sym• F^∨|_U) ≅ A^n_U.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exercise: show the sheaf of sections of this total space is isomorphic to F. This construction is the standard way to pass between vector bundles and their sheaves of sections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tautological bundle O(−1) on P^n as line subbundle of A^{n+1} (17.1.H)
rubrics_metrics.description: Over P^n_k, consider the subset X_k ⊂ A^{n+1}_k × P^n_k consisting of pairs (v, [x]) where v lies on the line corresponding to [x]; projection π : X_k → P^n_k is the tautological line bundle O(−1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use affine charts to compute transition functions and identify fibres with the corresponding lines. O(−1) is often called the tautological bundle and its dual is O(1).

rubrics_metrics.name: Relative Proj construction and gluing (17.2.C and 17.2.B)
rubrics_metrics.description: Given a quasicoherent graded O_X-algebra S satisfying reasonable hypotheses on each affine open, one can glue the affinely computed Proj constructions over an affine cover to form Proj_X S with structure morphism β : Proj_X S → X.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exercise 17.2.B gives the general gluing machinery: specify schemes over each affine open and compatible open embeddings on overlaps, satisfying natural compatibility; then glue to an X-scheme. The local Proj computations are the building blocks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hypotheses for using Proj effectively (17.2.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: To use Proj cleanly one typically requires: (i) S is generated in degree 1, and (ii) S_1 is finite type (i.e., the natural map Sym• O_X (S_1) → S is surjective and S_1 is finitely generated).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These hypotheses guarantee existence of an O(1) line bundle and that the Proj behaves like a projective bundle locally; one may check the surjectivity and finite generation affinely.

rubrics_metrics.name: Existence of O(1) on Proj under degree-1 finite-generation hypotheses (17.2.D)
rubrics_metrics.description: Under Hypotheses 17.2.1 (S generated in degree 1 and S_1 finite type), there is an invertible sheaf O_{Proj S}(1) on Proj_X S that restricts on each affine open Spec A to the usual O(1) on Proj_A S(Spec A).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Construct O(1) by gluing the local O(1)s; this invertible sheaf is crucial to relate Proj constructions to relatively very ample line bundles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proj commutes with base change (17.2.E)
rubrics_metrics.description: For S a graded quasicoherent O_X-algebra and ρ : Z → X any morphism, there is a natural isomorphism (Proj_Z ρ^*S, O(1)) ≅ (Z ×_X Proj_X S, ψ^* O_{Proj_X S}(1)) where ψ is the projection to Proj_X S.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This base-change compatibility is essential for checking properties after pulling back along morphisms and for working locally on the base.

rubrics_metrics.name: π-very ample (relative very ample) definition (17.2.2)
rubrics_metrics.description: Given a morphism π : X → Y, an invertible sheaf L on X is π-very ample if there exists a quasicoherent graded O_Y-algebra S (satisfying Hypotheses 17.2.1) with an isomorphism X ≅ Proj_Y S and L ≅ O(1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This defines very ampleness relative to a base Y: an L that realizes X as a Proj over Y and identifies L with the canonical O(1).

rubrics_metrics.name: Projectivization PF and P^n_X notation (17.2.3)
rubrics_metrics.description: For a finite-type quasicoherent sheaf F on X, Proj(Sym• F) is called the projectivization PF; if F is locally free of rank n+1, PF is a projective (P^n-) bundle over X. In particular P^n_X := P(O_X^{n+1}).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Projectivization behaves well under base change and is the relative version of projective space parameterizing lines in the fibers of F.
